thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary job 'realtime-text-gen-v2' failing 45% of requests in us-east-1 (slo_error_rate > 5% for 3m). auto-pager -> @ryan :rotating_light:
ryan: I'm on it. pulling up canary dashboard... link is blank? /dashboards/realtime/canary shows 502 errors with no graphs rendering. anyone else seeing an empty dashboard?
sara: yeah i'm seeing an empty panel too. looks like the dashboard tag 'canary-reads' got removed during the last dashboard PR?
miguel: can confirm, last infra deploy removed some grafana folder mounts. i rolled a change earlier that may have orphaned the dashboard path.
ash: (joined channel) is this customer impacting? alex, what are support queues saying?
alex: a couple of customers reported elevated 5xxs starting ~10m ago, mostly small-volume partners, not wide-scale yet. opening a quick incident ticket.
ryan: deploy-bot, what was the recent release in us-east-1?
deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.15-59 to service realtime-text-gen-v2 started at 1769504100. Canary traffic ramped to 10% at 1769504160.
ryan: that aligns. canary started failing right after the rollout. i'm going to pause the rollout and head for a kill switch if failures persist.
sara: i can't see the normal canary metrics (latency/error) in grafana, so we're blind. we only have alerts firing. the alert shows 45% errors but no traces.
miguel: i think the observability break is because the agent rollout also deployed a new collector config that filters canary metrics under a new tag. i'll revert the collector config now.
ash: do we have a fallback plan? can we toggle the feature flag to route traffic off the new variant?
ryan: yes, ff service 'realtime_v2' -> toggles. preparing to kill the feature for all canaries if errors don't drop in 2m.
alex: notifying affected customers: "We're seeing intermittent 5xxs on realtime endpoints; engineering is investigating; next update in 30m."
sara: quick note — our SLO burn panel is missing too. i can't confirm error budget consumption. this is risky for escalation.
miguel: collector revert in progress: applying patch cp-rollback-3.
(2m pause)
incident-bot: update: revert cp-rollback-3 applied at 1769504455. metric ingestion for canary tags resumed. some missing panels still need refresh.
sara: okay graphs are trickling in. error rate dropped from 45% -> 8% over last 3 minutes (still above threshold). latency p50 stable.
ryan: i'm going to flip the feature flag for canary routing to fallback variant while we triage to avoid further customer impact. ff command:
```
# kill canary variant for realtime_v2
ffctrl set realtime_v2 canary_variant=false --env us-east-1
```
ryan: executed. routing verified via logs: canary traffic dropped to 0.
ash: good. are pages silenced now? any noisy alerts to tidy up?
sara: alert flood reduced but we have a noisy duplicate alert that kept firing during the blank dashboard: alert 'canary_request_fail_rate' and legacy alert 'service_error_percent' both triggered. will consolidate.
amiguel: note for postmortem — dashboard mount change should have been in the infra PR checklist. i'm owning a follow-up.
alex: customer update sent: "We've rolled back canary routing and are investigating root cause, minor impact expected; we'll follow up in 1 hour."
ryan: creating incident ticket INC-176950 on PagerDuty, severity: P2 (partial degradation). handing over to sara for metrics restoration + root cause. i'm stepping off-call in 20m, ping miguel if anything else.
sara: taking over. immediate next actions: 1) confirm all canary dashboards fully restored, 2) collapse duplicate alerts, 3) run canary test job in staging with collector changes applied.
miguel: i'll add the dashboard mount revert to a hotfix changelist and run a sanity deploy to a single canary host.
deploy-bot: rollouts: paused. last successful stable revision: 2026.03.15-58.
sara: SLO note: error budget burn during this window ~0.07% — still within budget but we couldn't accurately measure for ~8 minutes due to missing panels. include that ambiguity in the postmortem.
alex: support will batch follow-ups for affected customers and provide incident summary after postmortem.
ryan: thanks team. small retrospective items: 1) alert deduping rule, 2) ensure dashboard mounts are tested as part of infra deploys, 3) add a canary-specific trace-export fallback so we don't go blind.
sara: logging action items in the incident doc now. tagging @miguel for infra follow-up and @ryan for flag rollback notes.
incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-176950 created by ryan at 1769504520. severity=P2. incident owner=sara.
miguel: following up — i'll submit infra PR to prevent dashboard path drift and add a unit test to validate grafana paths.
ash: adding a short runbook entry: if canary dashboards are empty, check collector tag mappings and revert to last known-good config.
sara: closing coordination: metrics restored, customer impact contained, rollout paused. leaving open until postmortem.
ryan: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
(reacts: :coffee: from alex, :eyes: from miguel, :white_check_mark: from sara)
